headline: Kai, Iran fired ballistic missiles at two U.S. warships and the Navy hit three of its tankers in reply — American markets are closed today; the oil market is not.
subline: Escalation in the Gulf, a Fed newly in its quiet period, and August CPI on Friday frame the short week.
asof: Labor Day · U.S. markets closed · strip is Friday's close; gold and bitcoin live as of 6:45 AM ET · every figure links to a source below

items.title: Hormuz risk premium meets a $90 barrel
items.sentence: WTI traded at $90.35 and Brent at $94.71 on Friday, each down about 1%, before a weekend that put missiles over the Gulf, per Forbes.

items.title: Payrolls tripled forecasts; short-end yields hit 52-week highs
items.sentence: August's 162,000 jobs against a 55,000 consensus — unemployment steady at 4.1% — pushed the 10-year to 4.78% and put a September hike squarely back in play, per TheStreet.

items.title: The Fed goes quiet; CPI lands Friday
items.sentence: The quiet period for the Sept. 15-16 meeting began Saturday, so August PPI on Thursday and CPI on Friday are the last major inputs before the decision, per Kiplinger.

items.title: Friday's dip still left the S&P up 12.8% for 2026
items.sentence: The index closed at 7,718.60, the Nasdaq at 26,506.99 and the Dow at 53,414.25 — losses of half a percent or less, per AP figures via LancasterOnline.

items.title: Gold eases to $4,412 in thin holiday trade
items.sentence: Gold trades at $4,412.30 Monday morning, down 0.46%, one of the few live U.S. prices on a market holiday, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Bitcoin gives back $80,000 after the jobs print
items.sentence: CoinDesk shows $79,682 this morning, with Friday's payrolls surprise cited as the driver of the slip back below $80,000. Flows cut both ways: holders have cashed out roughly 110,000 BTC while ETF inflows reached $3.8 billion over three weeks, the strongest stretch of 2026, per the same page.

items.title: U.S. strikes three Iranian tankers after missile attack
items.sentence: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at a carrier and a destroyer on Saturday; CENTCOM answered on three shadow-fleet tankers, with one crew abandoning ship and no American casualties, per NPR.

items.title: Peace shuttle reaches Kyiv after three hours with Putin
items.sentence: Witkoff and Kushner met Zelenskyy on Sunday after their Moscow session; he held to security guarantees as the price of any deal, and no breakthrough was announced, per NPR.

items.title: AfD takes commanding lead in German state election
items.sentence: Exit polls give the far-right party a clear lead in Sunday's state vote, with its route to actually governing still uncertain, per NPR.

items.title: Amazon cargo jet overruns Miami runway, killing five
items.sentence: The Boeing 767 freighter arriving from Puerto Rico ran off the runway at Miami International this weekend, killing five, per NPR.

items.title: Xi opens a rare swing: Kyrgyzstan, Egypt, India, America
items.sentence: The September tour, unusual for China's leader, is pitched as stable-partner diplomacy amid geopolitical uncertainty, per Foreign Exchanges' weekend roundup.

items.title: Jensen Huang declares 'AGI has arrived'
items.sentence: Nvidia's CEO credited GPT-6 Astra, trained on some 100,000 Grace Blackwell systems, and said 400,000 GPUs come online next, per his post on X.

items.title: UBS makes AI fluency an entry requirement
items.sentence: The bank will require incoming graduates and interns to demonstrate AI proficiency alongside their academics, per TechRadar.

items.title: Brokerages let retail wire AI agents to accounts
items.sentence: Platforms including Robinhood and Moomoo now let customers connect agents like Claude and Codex to execute strategies, a shift The Wall Street Journal covered this weekend, per AI Weekly.

items.title: Inspur's U.S. arm shipped $5.6 billion in chips
items.sentence: Aivres moved at least $5.6 billion of advanced U.S. technology to Southeast Asia since April 2024 — over $3 billion of it Blackwell computers — despite its parent's blacklisting, per Inside AI on NYT-reviewed trade records.

items.title: 'Model fatigue' sets in after a frenetic release run
items.sentence: With Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic all shipping new versions within weeks of one another, customers are struggling to keep up, per CNBC.
